targetText: Louis Blanc, the French socialist, won unenviable notriety during the revolution of 1848 by changing his stand from that of the class struggle to that of petty-bourgeois illusions, illusions adorned with would-be “socialist” phraseology, but in reality tending to strengthen the influence of the bourgeoisie over the proletariat.
explanation: Lenin defines Blancism: the historical tendency of moderate socialists to abandon independent class struggle, enter capitalist ministries, and peddle reformist delusions that subordinate the working class to the bourgeoisie.

targetText: Blancism has now gained the upper hand in Right-wing “Social-Democracy”, in the Organising Committee party in Russia.
explanation: Lenin identifies the Menshevik leadership of the Petrograd Soviet as modern Louis Blancs who formed a coalition bloc with the imperialist Provisional Government instead of taking state power for the Soviets.

targetText: The proletarian standpoint in this matter consists of a definite class characterisation of war, and of an irreconcilable hostility to imperialist war: that is, to a war between groups of capitalist countries (no matter whether monarchies or republics) for a division of capitalist spoils.
explanation: Lenin articulates the core Marxist-Leninist stance on world conflict: every war must be evaluated through the class interests driving it, rejecting all capitalist justifications regarding national defense when the conflict is an imperialist struggle for colonial markets and plunder.

targetText: The petty-bourgeois viewpoint differs from the bourgeois one (outright justification of the war, outright “defence of the fatherland”, i.e., defence of the interests of one’s own capitalists, defence of their “right” to annexations) in that the petty bourgeois “renounces” annexations, “condemns” imperialism, “demands” from the bourgeoisie that it cease to be imperialistic while keeping within the framework of world-imperialist relations and the capitalist system of economy.
explanation: Lenin lays bare the impotent moralism of petty-bourgeois pacifists who beg capitalist governments to stop behaving imperialistically without challenging the capitalist property relations that generate imperialist expansion.
